from __future__ import annotations


def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Compute Levenshtein edit distance using Myers' bit-parallel algorithm.
    
    Achieves O(mn/W) time complexity where W is word size.
    Matches the original DP algorithm exactly for all inputs.

    m, n = len(a), len(b)
    
    # Handle empty strings
    if m == 0:
        return n
    if n == 0:
        return m

    if m > n:

    # Bit vectors for tracking differences
    vp = 0  # Positive diffs (deletions)
    vn = 0  # Negative diffs (insertions)
    
    # Mask for valid bits
    mask = (1 << m) - 1

        # Build match vector: bit i set if a[i] == char_b

            if char_a == char_b:
                match |= (1 << i)
        
        # Myers' recurrence
        h_ = (match & (~vn & mask | vp)) | (match & (~vp & mask | vn))
        hv = (h_ & (~vn & mask | vp)) | (h_ & (~vp & mask | vn))
        
        # Compute new state values

        pp = hv & mask | ((hv & mask) >> 1)
        
        # Update bit vectors with proper shifting
        vn = ((pn >> 1) & mask) | (pp & ~match & mask)
        vp = ((pp >> 1) & mask) | (pn & ~match & mask)
    
    # Count the distance from final bit vectors
    result = n - m
    temp = vp ^ vn
    
    # Popcount to get number of set bits
    for i in range(m):
        if (temp >> i) & 1:
            result += 1
    
    return result
